research_question: Can multimodal large language models (M-LLMs), used as automated judges, reliably evaluate the safety of AI/ML-based brain MRI reconstruction methods — including via causal discovery and counterfactual diffusion-based simulation — compared to other safety-evaluation approaches?

framework.name: PICOS
framework.rationale: No clinical patient population is directly studied; PICOS is adapted so 'Population' is the class of AI reconstruction methods under evaluation, letting Comparator and Outcome capture the evaluation-methodology comparison this review is about, while Study design isolates methodological/technical contributions.

elements.name: Population
elements.value: AI/ML-based brain MRI reconstruction methods (any architecture: deep-learning accelerated, denoising, super-resolution, generative/diffusion-based reconstruction)

elements.name: Intervention
elements.value: Multimodal LLM (M-LLM) used as an automated judge, optionally combined with causal discovery and/or counterfactual diffusion-based simulation, to evaluate reconstruction safety

elements.name: Comparator
elements.value: Any alternative safety/quality evaluation approach — radiologist ground-truth review, pixel-wise metrics (SSIM/PSNR/LPIPS), other automated or LLM-based evaluators, or no comparator (proposing a new metric)

elements.name: Outcome
elements.value: Ability to detect/quantify reconstruction safety failures — hallucinated pathology, geometric/anatomical distortion, and other fidelity or trustworthiness failure modes

elements.name: Study design
elements.value: Methodological or technical contributions (new methods, benchmarks, evaluation frameworks); clinical-only studies without a technical evaluation contribution are out of scope

inclusion_criteria: Proposes or evaluates a method for assessing the safety, reliability, or fidelity of AI/ML-based MRI reconstruction (brain imaging, or general reconstruction methods clearly applicable to brain MRI)
Addresses at least one reconstruction failure mode: hallucinated/fabricated pathology, omitted true pathology, geometric or anatomical distortion, or related fidelity artifacts

Uses or evaluates LLM-as-judge, multimodal LLM evaluation, causal discovery, counterfactual simulation, or diffusion-based simulation as (part of) the evaluation methodology, OR is a closely comparable automated/human evaluation baseline
Peer-reviewed journal article, conference paper, or reputable preprint (arXiv/medRxiv) with a methodological or technical contribution
exclusion_criteria: Purely clinical study with no technical/methodological evaluation contribution
Animal-only or phantom-only studies with no relevance to human brain MRI
Editorial, letter, or commentary with no original methodology
Duplicate or superseded conference version where a fuller journal version exists
notes: Reviewer explicitly requested no date limit (overriding the tool's default latest-3-years window), given the fast-moving nature of M-LLMs and diffusion models. Comparator and safety-failure scope were deliberately kept broad per reviewer guidance ('all ML', 'all comparators', 'maybe all' failure modes) since this is framed as a review paper surveying the evaluation landscape, not a narrow technique comparison. Concept 4's term list was broadened (LLM*, large language model*, verb-form wildcards) since the exact phrase 'LLM-as-judge' would otherwise under-recall, and standalone 'LLM' was truncated to 'LLM*' to also catch plural/hyphenated forms in one term. Concept 4 was then switched to required:false (dropped from the AND-ed search) at the reviewer's request to broaden recall — the search is now (Brain MRI) AND (Reconstruction) AND (Safety/Fidelity Evaluation), catching general reconstruction-safety literature even when it doesn't mention LLMs/M-LLMs; the concept stays documented for reference/screening but no longer gates retrieval. This broadened PubMed's hit count from 156 to 24,692 (Scopus 8->127, Semantic Scholar 7->66), run into a separate folder from the narrow-search results.
reviewer_clarifications: Failure mode / safety definition -> hallucinated pathology, geometric/anatomical distortion, but broadened to cover the space since this is a review paper
Comparator -> all (radiologist ground truth, pixel-wise metrics, other automated methods)
Scope of reconstruction methods -> all AI/ML-based methods, not diffusion-specific
Eligible study types & timeframe -> methodological/technical papers only, no date limit
Broaden search -> drop LLM-as-Judge concept from the required AND to widen recall

_meta.question: M-LLM-as-a-Judge: Causal Discovery and Counterfactual Diffusion Simulation for Evaluating Brain MRI Reconstruction Safety
